comment: Owners withdrawn from routine work: both bounded search axes are spent and the owner still does not reproduce. Data for the check, not documentation -- it keeps a small number of owners out of the queue without putting a record of dead ends in front of every contributor. An entry is removed the moment its owner becomes exact. The opposite register is exact/provisional.json, which holds owners that DO match but whose source was written toward the bytes.

unmatchable.reason: Blocked on the store merge, not on a reading. The reference writes three consecutive words as `stmia rB!, {r0, r1, r2}` and then `subs rB, #12`, undoing the writeback into a register that is dead at the next instruction. gcc 2.96 Thumb cannot emit that: the store_multiple peepholes in arm.md are TARGET_ARM only, and Thumb's sole multi-register store is the block move, which always pairs stmia with an ldmia from memory -- a by-value struct already sitting in r1-r3 is spilled to the stack and reloaded before the stmia. old_agbcc does the same. So no C source reaches this sequence, and no compiler emits a dead compensating subs; it reads as a hand-written kick macro. The remaining differences here are the register assignment that ascending-order merge forces, downstream of the same cause.

Comparison canonicalisation, not a reading. The reference tests `cmp #9 / blt` and stock gcc 2.96 always canonicalises this to `cmp #8 / ble`. Measured on the owner: `!(w < 9)`, `9 <= w`, `w > 8` and `!(9 > w)` all compile to the identical two halfwords, and `w - 9 >= 0` is far worse at 35. There is no source spelling that reaches the reference form and no stock switch for it -- this fork once invented `-fno-canonicalize-comparison` for exactly this, and it is gone.

If-conversion, not a reading. The source computes `(*flags & 1) ? 17 : 16` and gcc's ce pass makes it branchless (`negs / orrs / lsrs #31 / adds #16`) where the reference branches. Writing it as an explicit if/else changes nothing -- gcc canonicalises both to the same RTL -- and stock gcc 2.96 has no if-conversion switch: `-fno-if-conversion` and `-fno-cond-exec` are gcc 3.x options and cc1 here rejects them. This fork once invented `-fthumb-no-if-convert` for it.
The reference orders the counter increment before the volatile store and the argument load after it; the emitted pair is transposed.
